problem: Issue #656: when GitHub rate-limits a pull request check lookup, Shaka reports "GitHub returned invalid JSON." with no HTTP status. gh pr checks exits 1 both for failing checks and for its own errors, and Shaka parsed the empty stdout of the second case as JSON. Root cause: check_list.rb accepted exit 1 as a normal result and sent empty stdout to parse_json, which discarded stderr and its HTTP status.
audience: Agents and maintainers who read check evidence from shaka pr, pr watch, handoff, and merge.
outcome: A rate-limited or missing pull request check lookup reports the real gh failure and its HTTP status instead of an invalid-JSON error. Scope: one method's empty-stdout branch in github/check_list.rb, the status passed through required_checks, and focused tests. Leaves out: raw gh stderr stays out of error messages; exit 0 with empty stdout keeps the JSON error. Safe because: non-empty stdout and the no-checks diagnostics take the same paths as before; only a failure that already raised now raises with its real cause.
validation: Rate-limit reproduction failed before the fix and passes after: .agents/shaka/bin/test test/github_unprotected_check_list_test.rb (10 runs, 0 failures). Full local validation passed on this head: .agents/shaka/bin/validate (3454 tests, 0 failures; RuboCop clean). Live call through the real gh runner for missing PR 999999 raises `gh pr 999999 failed (exit 1).` instead of the JSON error. Not verified: a live rate limit was not triggered; the test uses the issue's stderr, and a GraphQL rate-limit message without (HTTP nnn) would still have a nil status.
repair_history: One local review round: one finding that empty stdout with exit 8 is not directly tested, documented as a nit. No other repairs.
